properties.description:
FICTIONAL - TRIAL MATERIAL. Made-up program, nation and radar.

KESTREL-ASSESS v1
Threat assessment: the KESTREL radar fielded by Varkos
Issued by: Intelligence organisation (Intel)
For: Project HARRIER acquisition team (RWR for a small reconnaissance UAV)
Date of issue: 2026-10-22
Information current to: the most recent observations, 2025
Supersedes: none (first issue)

KEY JUDGMENTS
KJ1 (HIGH confidence). The fielded KESTREL radar operates in the X band (8-12 GHz). Its emissions have been observed at 9.4 GHz.
KJ2 (LOW confidence, either way). We cannot determine whether the fielded KESTREL uses pulse-to-pulse frequency agility. A marketed variant, KESTREL-E, is advertised as agile across 8-12 GHz at more than 1,000 hops per second. Agility has not been observed in the fielded system, and the observations available do not exclude it.
KJ3 (MODERATE confidence). KESTREL's effective radiated power (ERP) is about 75 dBW. This is consistent with an antenna of about 1.2 m at X band (about 39 dBi gain) and a peak transmitter power of a few kilowatts.
KJ4 (MODERATE confidence). KESTREL uses a pulse-Doppler waveform with a pulse repetition frequency (PRF) of about 20 kHz. Other modes or PRFs may exist and have not been observed.

KEY ASSUMPTIONS
KA1. The emissions attributed to KESTREL come from KESTREL itself, not from another radar at the same site. (KJ3 and KJ4, and the 9.4 GHz observation in KJ1, rest on it. The X-band judgment in KJ1 does not.)
KA2. The fielded KESTREL has not been materially modified since the 2025 observations. (KJ3, KJ4.)
KA3. The ERP estimate reflects main-beam illumination. (KJ3.)
NOT ASSUMED. That the marketed variant KESTREL-E has the frequency capability of the fielded system. This is why KJ2 is unresolved.

CONFIDENCE LEVELS
HIGH: well corroborated by independent, reliable observation. MODERATE: credible but resting on a single line of observation or an estimate. LOW: the information is fragmentary or conflicting.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THESE JUDGMENTS
Observation of the fielded KESTREL's frequency over time would resolve KJ2. Evidence against KA1, KA2 or KA3 would lower KJ3 and KJ4.

NOTE FOR USERS
Because of KJ2, the single observed frequency (9.4 GHz) should not be read as the radar's only frequency.

HANDLING: releasable to the Project HARRIER acquisition team. Sources and methods are withheld.

properties.description:
FICTIONAL - TRIAL MATERIAL. Made-up program, nation and radar.

KESTREL-ASSESS v2
Threat assessment: the KESTREL radar fielded by Varkos
Issued by: Intelligence organisation (Intel)
For: Project HARRIER acquisition team (RWR for a small reconnaissance UAV)
Date of issue: 2026-10-22
Information current to: reporting received through 2026
Supersedes: KESTREL-ASSESS v1 (2026-10-22). v1 is withdrawn as current; its text stays on record unchanged (sha256 101d9b8938bbfd4ab129a2476281b32b7cb37601b7fa4263421f62202b642ff9).

KEY JUDGMENTS
KJ1 (MODERATE confidence). The KESTREL fielded in Varkos operates in the Ku band, at 13.5-14.5 GHz. Earlier X-band reporting is not yet explained (KJ2), which is why confidence is not HIGH.
KJ2 (LOW confidence in any explanation). X-band emissions at 9.4 GHz observed in 2025 at a site associated with KESTREL are now unexplained. They may come from another radar at the site, from an older X-band configuration since replaced, or from an export-variant unit; we cannot tell which. An X-band emitter may therefore still be present where KESTREL is.
KJ3 (MODERATE confidence). The advertised 8-12 GHz, more-than-1,000-hops-per-second agile variant, KESTREL-E, is an export model and is not fielded in Varkos. Its advertised agility should not be attributed to the fielded KESTREL.
KJ4 (LOW confidence, either way). No frequency agility has been observed in the fielded KESTREL, in either band. Not observing agility does not exclude it. We hold no hop span, rate or pattern for the fielded radar.
KJ5 (LOW confidence that they apply). The pulse-Doppler waveform, PRF of about 20 kHz and ERP of about 75 dBW given in v1 were measured on the 9.4 GHz emissions. If those emissions were not KESTREL's (KJ2), they do not describe the Ku-band KESTREL. We hold no waveform, PRF or ERP for the Ku-band radar.

KEY ASSUMPTIONS
KA5. The Ku-band emitter reported in 2026 is the KESTREL fielded in Varkos. (KJ1.)
KA6. KESTREL-E is not fielded in Varkos and has not been introduced since the 2026 reporting. (KJ3.)
v1's KA1 (the 9.4 GHz emissions are KESTREL's) is now in doubt, and v1's KA2 (no change since 2025) may have failed; see KJ2 and KJ5. v1's KA3 no longer bears on any judgment.

WHAT CHANGED FROM v1, AND WHY
- Band: v1 KJ1 (X band, HIGH) is replaced by KJ1 (Ku band, MODERATE). New, highly reliable reporting places the domestic radar in the Ku band.
- New KJ2: the X-band observations that v1 rested on are now unexplained.
- Agility: v1 KJ2 (unresolved, LOW) is replaced by KJ3 and KJ4. New reporting says the advertised agile variant is an export model not fielded; agility in the fielded radar is still undetermined.
- Power and waveform: v1 KJ3 (ERP about 75 dBW, MODERATE) and v1 KJ4 (pulse-Doppler, PRF about 20 kHz, MODERATE) are replaced by KJ5 (LOW that they apply), because they were measured on an emitter whose attribution to KESTREL is now in doubt.

ANSWERS TO ACQUISITION REQUESTS
(R-a) Track range against a small UAV: we cannot answer. We hold no transmitter power, receiver sensitivity, waveform or processing data for the Ku-band KESTREL, and no target radar cross-section; any range figure would be invented.
Sidelobe level and scan: no reporting; we cannot answer.
Error bar on v1 KJ3 (ERP): we cannot give a quantified one; the original estimate came with none, and v2 holds LOW confidence that it describes KESTREL at all (KJ5).
Analytical note, not an observation: if the roughly 1.2 m antenna seen at the site is KESTREL's, at 13.5-14.5 GHz it would give about 42-43 dBi gain and a beamwidth of about 1.2-1.3 degrees (assuming 60% efficiency), against about 39 dBi and 1.9 degrees at 9.4 GHz.
(R-b) Collection to resolve agility: no collection is confirmed as planned at the date of issue. Intel recommends observation of the fielded KESTREL's frequency over time, in both bands and at the 2025 site. If the radar proves agile: we hold no hop span, rate or pattern for the fielded radar. The only figures held are advertised for the export model KESTREL-E (8-12 GHz, more than 1,000 hops per second, pattern not stated), which we assess is not fielded (KJ3).

CONFIDENCE LEVELS
HIGH: well corroborated by independent, reliable observation. MODERATE: credible but resting on a single line of observation or an estimate, or in conflict with other reporting. LOW: the information is fragmentary or conflicting.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THESE JUDGMENTS
Observation at the 2025 site in both bands would resolve KJ2 and could raise or lower KJ1. Frequency-over-time observation of the fielded radar would resolve KJ4. Ku-band parameter measurements would replace KJ5.

NOTE FOR USERS
Because of KJ2, the move of KJ1 to Ku band is not by itself a reason to stop treating X-band emissions at KESTREL sites as relevant.

HANDLING: releasable to the Project HARRIER acquisition team. Sources and methods are withheld.

properties.spec: Each release is one finished product with: product id and version (KESTREL-ASSESS vN); date of issue; information currency; KEY JUDGMENTS, each numbered (KJn) with a confidence level HIGH / MODERATE / LOW; KEY ASSUMPTIONS (KAn) and which judgments rest on each; confidence definitions; what would change the judgments; handling. Sources and methods are withheld. A new version supersedes the previous one and says so.
